text:
mike: heads up — seeing ~7 pods stuck Pending in us-west-2 GPU pool since ~08:10. CA didn't scale and scheduler says 0/4 nodes available: node(s) didn't match taints/nodeSelector.
sara: can you paste the pod yaml or `kubectl describe`?
mike: `kubectl describe` shows: 'Tolerations: <none>' but our deployment manifest has a toleration key `gpu` — weird. here's the manifest we deploy:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
        - key: "gpu"
          operator: "Equal"
          value: "dedicated"
          effect: "NoSchedule"
      nodeSelector:
        workload: "inference"
```
jonathan: i touched taint keys in the us-west-2 rollout last night — changed the node taint to `redwood/gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule` to support multi-tenant tagging. i forgot to update the older manifests. sorry, my bad.
lina: that explains it — autoscaler log shows "scale-up rejected: no candidate nodes match pod requirements" which is CA refusing to create nodes because pods require a taint that doesn't exist on any nodegroup. CA won't help unless either the pod tolerates the new taint or the nodegroups have the old taint.
oliver: quick remedial options: (1) patch deployments to add toleration for `redwood/gpu`, (2) add a temporary node taint with old key on burst pools, or (3) change CA expander + flags to allow scale-up of nodegroup with matching resources. fastest is patching the deployment.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scaleUp: rejected for 3 pods: no matching nodegroup for required taints (reason: TaintMismatch)
sara: mike — do the manifests come from the helm chart? we can inject toleration in values v1.3.2 and do a quick release.
mike: manifests come from helm chart `inference-service`, yes. i'll patch the live deployments first to unblock then cut a chart PR. patch command i used:
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch deploy inference-service --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations/-","value":{"key":"redwood/gpu","operator":"Equal","value":"dedicated","effect":"NoSchedule"}}]'
```
jonathan: after patch, pods started scheduling onto burst-gpu pool within ~40s. :thumbsup:
lina: follow-up: we should normalize taint keys across clusters and update the admission webhook that injects nodeSelectors/tolerations for inference workloads. put a migration ticket and a small rollout plan (with canary). CA config note: `--balance-similar-node-groups` helps in some cases, but it won't fix taint mismatches.
oliver: filing INFRA-3427 to standardize taint keys + update runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-scheduling
mike: ok — patched 3 deployments, will open the chart PR and a migration playbook. thanks everyone.
sara: nice quick fix. also add a short test to our e2e job that verifies a pod with new toleration can schedule to burst pools.
jonathan: will follow up on the taint rename docs and add a note to release checklist so this doesn't slip again. :eyes:
mike: closing thread when PR + ticket exist.
